title: Delegation Model Crosswalk (STD-07 records to STD-08 objects)
description: A field-by-field mapping between the two object models the delegation standards publish. STD-07 (https://ethotechnics.org/api/schema/revisable-delegation-record.schema.json) models a delegation as an append-only stream of records, each with a kind and a kind-specific content block. STD-08 models the same delegation as a set of long-lived state objects: an authority grant, a capability catalog, a policy record, an intervention specification, and, where Part D §4.4 draws on the deployment, a dependency record. Neither model is derivable from the other by name alone, and STD-08 clauses cite STD-07 clauses, so this document states which field corresponds to which, where the semantics differ, and where one model has no counterpart at all. It is descriptive: it declares an existing correspondence, it does not require either side to change. Relations are read left to right, from the STD-07 field to the STD-08 field.

relations.equivalent: The two fields carry the same information in the same shape. A value can be moved across without loss.
relations.structured_refinement: The STD-08 field carries the same information in a structured form where STD-07 uses free text. Moving right to left is lossless; moving left to right requires a person or a parser to impose the structure.
relations.partial: The STD-08 field carries part of what the STD-07 field carries, or carries it only for some values. Round-tripping loses information.
relations.split: One STD-07 field corresponds to more than one STD-08 field, and which one depends on the value.
relations.no_counterpart: The field exists in one model and has nothing corresponding in the other. Recorded so that an implementer does not invent an equivalence.

mappings.note: STD-07 scope is a single free-text string with minLength 1. STD-08 splits the same boundary into a structured scope object (action_classes, systems, populations, limits) plus a separate action_classes list holding the subset currently authorized. A STD-08 grant therefore distinguishes the boundary of the lease from what is live inside it; STD-07 does not, so a scope string cannot be mechanically decomposed into the two.

STD-07 holder is a bare string. STD-08 grantee is an object with id and a type drawn from agent, role, system, human. The id corresponds to the holder string; the type has no STD-07 source on the authorization record and must be supplied, though the actor.kind of the record that emitted the authorization is often the same distinction.

STD-07 granted_by is a bare string naming the grantor. STD-08 issuing_authority is a contact object (name, role, contact) because Part A requires the issuer to be reachable to renew, narrow, or revoke. The grant's provenance block (issued_by, issued_at, basis_summary) carries the issue event itself, which on the STD-07 side lives on the record envelope (time.recorded_at, summary) rather than in content.

Same field, same enum: unattended, confirm, forbidden. Added to the grant so that STD-08 §3.2 (confirm mode must carry intervention_ref) can be checked against a single object. Do not confuse it with grant state: mode is how much autonomy the delegation carries, state is whether it is currently in force.

STD-07 ceiling is one free-text bound (a spend, a count, a blast radius, a duration). STD-08 carries the same bounds as scope.limits, a keyed map of named limits with string, number, or boolean values. One STD-07 ceiling string commonly becomes several named limits.

STD-07 expires_at is always a date-time. STD-08 until accepts either a date-time or a plain-language lapse condition. Every STD-07 expires_at maps to an until; an until holding a condition has no STD-07 counterpart in content and would have to be written as an invalidated_by condition instead. The record envelope's time.valid_until is a different thing: it marks the record stale, not the lease lapsed.
Both are arrays of free-text conditions and both are required, on the same reasoning: a delegation with no revocation conditions is a transfer, not a delegation (STD-07 §2.2).

STD-07 depends_on is one flat list of record_ids, undifferentiated by what kind of thing is depended on. STD-08 splits it by kind: dependence on a policy becomes a pinned entry in policy_refs and usually also an evidence_basis entry; dependence on a belief or an evidence item becomes an evidence_basis entry (ref, summary, as_of); dependence on a capability becomes capability_catalog_ref plus the catalog entry's own state. Which STD-08 field a depends_on entry belongs in cannot be decided from the id alone — see the identifier-convention gap below.

STD-07 invalidated_by holds checkable conditions, each optionally with a check URI and an ISO 8601 clock. STD-08 assumptions are the propositions taken to be true at issue time, stated positively; their negations are the invalidation conditions. The mapping is a negation, not a copy, and it is lossy in both directions: STD-08 assumptions carry no check URI and no clock, so the clock STD-07 §3.3 relies on is not representable on the grant. Conditions that would end the lease rather than merely reopen it belong in revocation_conditions.

Same field, same enum: absent, configured, verified, broken. STD-07 §3.4 makes the configured/verified line load-bearing and STD-08 Part A relies on it without restating it, so the catalog entry now carries the state the gate is evaluated against.

Both are stable identifiers for one capability. The STD-07 record identifies the capability inside the emitting system's stream; the catalog entry identifies it inside a catalog that a grant references by catalog_id.

STD-07 requires lists prerequisite capability ids. STD-08 tools lists the tool, API, or integration names the capability is reachable through. They overlap where the prerequisite is a tool and diverge where it is another capability; a prerequisite capability has no catalog field and is representable only as a separate catalog entry.

STD-07 contest declares who may object, where, and within what reversal clock. The intervention specification answers a different question — what the named human can actually see, prevent, and alter — and only its owner, on_disagreement, and reach_time_target overlap with contest. STD-08 §3.1 exists precisely because contest does not establish that an oversight claim is a control.

No STD-07 counterpart. An STD-07 authorization has no lifecycle field: it is a record, and it stops holding when a later record supersedes it or an invalidated_by condition fires. STD-08 grant state (allowed, review_required, suspended, revoked) is a standing property of a live object, and review_required in particular — the burden of proof shifted back to the issuer, with the grant neither in force nor withdrawn — has nothing to correspond to on the record side. Do not map it onto mode.

No STD-07 counterpart as a field. STD-07 reconstructs history from the record stream itself: supersedes links, revision records, and the ordering of the integrity chain. The information is comparable but it lives in the log rather than on the object, and a state_history transition reason (issued, renewal, expansion, evidence_changed, policy_review, challenge, incident, expiry, manual) has no STD-07 vocabulary to map to. Expansion in particular, which STD-08 §1.3 and §1.4 make a distinct authorization decision, would appear in STD-07 only as a new authorization record superseding an earlier one.

No STD-07 counterpart. STD-07 has one severity of failure: a condition either invalidates the record or it does not. STD-08 distinguishes conditions that move a grant to review_required from conditions that suspend or revoke it. Mapping review_conditions onto invalidated_by would overstate them, since an STD-07 invalidation condition ends the record's hold rather than reopening its justification.

No STD-07 counterpart. STD-07 records expiry but says nothing about what a renewal must show; that is exactly the gap STD-08 Part A fills. A renewal under STD-07 alone is indistinguishable from re-issuing the same authorization record.

Policy records have no STD-07 record kind. The STD-07 kind enum is belief, capability, authorization, action, discrepancy, revision, objection, outcome; a policy is none of them. The nearest available shape is a belief record whose content.proposition states the policy and whose invalidated_by carries the review triggers, but that mapping is not an equivalence: a belief has no version, no status enum, and no expires_at, and STD-08 §2.1 requires all three. An institution emitting STD-07 records cannot represent Part B faithfully without extending the kind enum, which is a change to STD-07 and is not made here.

No STD-07 counterpart. STD-07 records what a delegation is and what invalidates it; it carries nothing about whether the institution could still correct after the fact. Every STD-07 field is about the delegation's validity — its scope, its holder, its ceiling, its expiry, the conditions that would end it — and none of them asks what happens once a permitted action has already gone wrong. correction_capacity is a standing, timestamped statement of the institution's own capacity, assessed against the scope in force, and there is no record field it can be read out of. Do not map it onto invalidated_by or revocation_conditions: those end the delegation, they do not repair what it did.

No STD-07 counterpart. STD-07 has a discrepancy record kind, but a discrepancy is a report that something diverged after someone noticed; it is not a statement that divergence can be noticed at all, and it names no evaluator. The record envelope's actor identifies who emitted a record, not who evaluates whether actions were wrong, so the independence question STD-08 §4.1 makes load-bearing — whether the party evaluating the process is the party executing it — cannot be asked of an STD-07 stream at all. Do not read actor.kind as an evaluator.

This is the one genuine overlap, and it is partial in a specific way. STD-07 contest carries standing (who may object), channel (where an objection is accepted), and reversal_clock (the ISO 8601 duration inside which an accepted objection owes a revision or a reasoned refusal). Those correspond one-for-one to the assertion side of three of the seven components: standing to correction_capacity.standing, channel to correction_capacity.challenge, reversal_clock to the clock in correction_capacity.review. What does not carry across is the demonstration: each STD-08 component is a present/evidence pair, so it records whether the route was exercised and what shows it, while contest declares that the route exists. A record can satisfy contest in full while all three components are present false. contest also names no examiner, only a clock, so the named party half of correction_capacity.review has no source in it. Moving right to left keeps the declaration and loses the evidence; moving left to right yields components whose evidence must be supplied from outside the record.

No STD-07 counterpart for any of the three. STD-07 §4.2 obliges an answer to an accepted objection, and a revision record is how the answer is written down, but nothing in the record model states in advance that the examiner holds the authority to change the grant, that the affected state can be returned, or that the institution can absorb the reversal and keep operating. The first is a fact about the examiner's powers, the second about the system's state machine, the third about the institution's finances and staffing; STD-07 records outcomes, not standing capacities, so a stream of revision records shows that corrections have happened without establishing that the next one could. operable_after_correction in particular is evidenced from the dependency record under §4.4, which is outside the record model entirely.

No STD-07 counterpart. These three fields say that a preserved capacity has moved — retained, degrading, or lost as observed, and replenished, unchanged, or consumed since the previous assessment — because correction capital depreciates between assessments unless it is deliberately replenished. STD-07 records events, and depreciation is not an event: nothing is emitted on the day a rehearsal stops happening. The nearest available shape, a belief record whose proposition asserts the capacity and whose invalidated_by names its lapse, still needs someone to notice the lapse and emit a discrepancy, which is exactly the noticing these fields exist to make unnecessary. Read the trio as a per-capacity delta, not as a score: statuses do not average, and one lost capacity is not offset by two retained ones.

No STD-07 counterpart, and the same gap as grant.correction_capacity.detection one level up: this is the deployment-level counterpart to correction_capacity.detection.independent_of_executor, asking of the whole deployment who evaluates whether it is going wrong and whether that party is independent of the party that runs it. STD-07 identifies the emitting system and actor of each record but has no field for an evaluating party and therefore no way to state, or to deny, independence from the executor.

known_gaps.summary: STD-07 record_ids and STD-08 object ids do not share a convention, so an STD-08 object cannot be referenced from a STD-07 depends_on without an ad-hoc mapping.
known_gaps.detail: STD-07 §5.3 recommends record_id of the form <system>:<kind>:<local-id>, for example whether:authorization:2026-w36, and the kind segment is what tells a reader which record shape to expect. STD-08 objects use flat identifiers with no system and no kind segment: GRANT-2026-0142, CAT-RISK-OPS-V2-2026-07, POL-FRAUD-HOLD-3.2, INT-RISK-STEWARD-1. A STD-07 depends_on entry is defined as a list of record_ids, so putting a flat grant or policy id in it produces a reference that resolves only if the reading system already knows which model the id belongs to. This document records the mismatch rather than resolving it: silently rewriting Line A ids into the STD-07 form would break every existing cross-reference between the published examples, and adding a translation table here would be a convention no clause requires. Closing it needs a decision in one of the two standards — either STD-07 relaxes depends_on to accept typed external references, or STD-08 object ids adopt the <system>:<kind>:<local-id> form. As of 2026-09-07 the STD-07 side is actively revising this space: the record's system block gained an optional instance segment so a consumer can tell which deployment of a system emitted a record, after two environments running the same model emitted identical record ids for the same subject. That is a different problem from this one, and it does not close it, but it locates the fix: the convention is live on the record side, so a shared form should be settled there rather than by reshaping STD-08 object ids to match a moving target.

known_gaps.summary: The ISO 8601 clock STD-07 attaches to an invalidation condition has no field on the authority grant.
known_gaps.detail: STD-07 invalidated_by[].clock bounds how long a matching discrepancy may go unanswered, and STD-07 §3.3 makes silence past the clock a governance failure. The grant's assumptions, review_conditions, and revocation_conditions are plain strings with no clock and no check URI. STD-08 §2.3 and §2.4 do speak of a trigger's declared clock, but the only place a clock is actually typed is the policy record's review_triggers, so a grant-level condition that is not inherited from a policy carries no deadline anywhere in the Line A model.

known_gaps.summary: STD-07 action, outcome, and discrepancy records have no standing STD-08 object.
known_gaps.detail: STD-08 models what a delegation must show while it stands, not what it did. The decision record is the closest Line A object to an STD-07 action record, but it is a decision about one subject rather than a record of an act and its result, and there is no Line A object at all for outcome or discrepancy. Those record kinds are therefore left unmapped here rather than being attached to the nearest-looking object.

known_gaps.summary: STD-07 records what a delegation is and what invalidates it, and carries nothing about whether the institution could still correct after the fact, so six of the seven components of correction capacity have no record field to read out of.
known_gaps.detail: The asymmetry is structural rather than an omission of detail. STD-07 fields answer whether a delegation holds: scope, holder, grantor, mode, ceiling, expiry, revocation conditions, the conditions that would invalidate the record, and the objection route in contest. Correction capacity answers a different question — supposing an action taken under the delegation was wrong, could the institution notice, hear the objection, examine it, change the grant, return the affected state, and still operate. Only contest touches that question, and only its assertion side (see record.contest.correction_components). Closing the gap is not a matter of adding fields to a record: capacity is a standing property of the institution at a point in time, assessed against the scope in force, which is why STD-08 puts it on the grant with an assessed_at and STD-06 puts the deployment half on the dependency record. An institution emitting STD-07 records alone cannot show Law IV's proportionality, because the ratio of scope to capacity has no record-side denominator.
